弥源太
「そして、帯刀タテワキの儀によって結縁した武者と
劔冑は常に一体……。
　復元の力は武者の肉体にも及ぶのだ。この
ようにな」



ふき
「そうなんだ……。
　すごい……」



景明
「さりながら。
　貴方がたがお助けくださらなければ、回復
するより前に命を絶たれていたことでしょう。
やはり御礼は申し上げねばなりません」



弥源太
「なれは代官だのその取巻きだのに殺される
ような天命ほしではないよ。
　それに御堂、うては当然のことをしている
に過ぎん」



景明
「……」



弥源太
「なれが山の作業場であの馬鹿者を止めてく
れた折、うてもその場におった。
　我が村の救い主が倒れているのを見掛けて、
何もせぬ法があろうか」



景明
「それは一身上の都合でした事。
　救いなどと考えられては身が縮みます」



弥源太
「だとしても助けられれば感謝はするもの。
　当然のことであろう？」



景明
「……」

en: I was beginning to feel like nothing more than a green youth being stubborn for the sake of it. One feels the difference in years.
ja:
なんだか自分がただ強情を張っている未熟な若造に
しか思えなくなってきた。
　人生経験の差を感じる。

en:
Kageaki"Elder... forgive me. That is how you appear to me, but perhaps I am mistaken?"

弥源太"You are not, young man. I have counted fifty years. For an Emishi, that is old, very old. About the age at which they start calling a man elder."
ja:
景明
「御老人……失礼。
　そのようにお見受けしたのですが、もしや
見込み違いということは」



弥源太
「ないよ、お若い方。
　歳はもう五十を数えた。蝦夷としては老人
も老人、長老などと呼ばれる頃合かな」

en:
As I had thought. True to the ageless Emishi, he looked at most a man in his prime. But the weight in every movement, and the address he used, Mido, told his real age.

Mido is an old-fashioned honorific for warriors, which few people use any more. It comes from the fact that the court's warriors' hall once stood in a building called Shakutendo.
ja:
やはり、か。
　不老の蝦夷種族らしく、外見上はいいところ壮年に
しか達していない。しかし動作の端々にある重さと、
御堂という呼び方が実際の歳を窺わせた。

　御堂とはもう用いる者も多くはない、武者に対する
古風な敬称。
　かつて宮中の武者溜りが釈天堂という建物にあった
ことを由来とする。

en:
Kageaki"Then, Elder, you belong to the clan said to perform rites on this mountain."

弥源太"The headman told you, I suppose. The last descendants of that clan are these three in this room."

弥源太"I am Yagenta. These are my granddaughters. The bigger one is Fuki, the small one Funa."

Kageaki"I should have introduced myself sooner. Kageaki Minato, of the Kamakura Police."

景明
「では、御老人。
　貴方はやはり、この山で祭祀を行っておら
れるというご一族の」




弥源太
「村長にでも聞いたか。
　その一族の最後の末裔がここにおる三人よ」

弥源太
「うては弥源太。
　こやつらは孫で、大きい方がふき、小さい

景明
「申し遅れました。
　鎌倉警察署の湊斗景明です」

I bowed my head, though with fresh bandages being wound around me I could not manage full etiquette.

The elder answered with a slight dip of the chin. The older granddaughter bowed over and over in alarm, and the younger one just beamed at me again. The little one seemed the more dignified of the two, which amused me somewhat.

　……新しい包帯を巻かれながらでは、充分な礼儀を

　老人は軽く顎を引きだけして応えた。
　孫の方を見ると、上の娘は恐縮した風で何度も礼を

en:
弥源太"So you are police, then."

Kageaki"I am grateful for your cooperation. This debt I will certainly repay later..."

Kageaki"For today, I will take my leave shortly."

ふき"Eh!? But— you cannot! Impossible!"

弥源太"...I praised your recovery earlier. Even so, for a night you will not be moving. Force the body and the wound opens again."

Kageaki"But I cannot impose on you. If I stay, this body will not only take up floor space—"

弥源太"You are worried about the magistrate's men? I see. So that wound came from a fight with them, and you think pursuers may follow."

Kageaki"Precisely."

弥源太"That worry is unnecessary. Suppose we throw you out. These men stop troubling us, is it?"

Kageaki"That is..."

弥源太"As long as they are here, trouble is here for the village. Personal reasons or whatever reasons, Mido, if you are going to deal with them, helping you benefits the village."

Kageaki"..."

弥源太"Rest here one full day. For a man like you, that should likely be enough for a full recovery."

ふき"Please, stay. Difficult matters I don't understand, but injured like this and walking out—no, that is not allowed."

ふな"Hmm? Didi, what happened to Bhaiya?"

ふき"Bhaiya says he wants to go home."

ふな"Nooo! I don't like that! I want him to stay more..."

ふき"Right? See, warrior sahib? Even Funa says so."

景明

　流石に一晩は動けんだろうよ。無理をして

景明
「しかし、ご迷惑は掛けられません。
　自分がここに留まれば、この図体で場所を

弥源太
「代官どものことを案じておるのか？
　なるほど……やはりその傷はやつらと一戦

弥源太

　一身上の都合だろうが何だろうが、御堂、
なれがやつらを成敗するというのなら、なれ
を助けることは村の利益に適う」




景明
「……」




弥源太
「丸一日はここで休んでゆけ。
　なれならば、おそらくそれで全快しよう」




ふき
「そうしてください。

こんな大怪我をしている人が出ていくなんて、

ふな
「んーっ？

ふき
「にーや、おうちに帰りたいんだって」




ふな

ふき
「そうよねっ。

en:
Being told that was no argument. ...Still, I could not see myself pushing through the pair of them and leaving.

And as Elder Yagenta said, forcing myself out now offered neither advantage nor reason. Accepting their kindness seemed the wiser course.

言われても。
　……しかし、これを振り切って行くことはできそう
になかった。

　それに弥源太老人の言う通り、今無理を押して出て
いく選択にはどうも利もなければ理もないらしい。
　ここは厚意に甘えておくのが賢明だろうか。

Kageaki"...Understood. I shall be a trouble to you."

Muramasa《Please take care of us.》

ふき"Wah! The tingly voice came!"

ふな"Tingly-tingly!"

弥源太"............"

景明
「……わかりました。
　ご厄介をおかけします」




村正
《よろしく》



ふき
「わっ、ぴりぴりきたー！」




ふな
「ぴりぴりー！」






弥源太
「…………」

en:
小太郎"............"

長坂"Well? Speak, Kotaro..."

小太郎"Two sets of footprints. Somebody has picked up our fallen gentleman, it seems."

長坂"Oh...?"

小太郎"Any guess who? Not many people pass through such a place by accident, no?"

長坂"There is one. ...That fellow. Forever a nuisance, that man."

小太郎"..."

長坂"We climb the mountain. Go round the back."

小太郎"Aye. Really now... hard going for an old man."

「…………」




長坂
「どうよ。
　小太郎……」

　どうやら、誰ぞに拾われたようだの」

　このような場所を通りがかる者などに……」




長坂

男よ」

長坂

小太郎

en:
Emishi is the name of one of Yamato's minority peoples.

They live in small communities scattered throughout the country. In general, the nearer the northeast, the larger and more numerous the communities become. Elsewhere, too, they concentrate in famous smithing districts, such as Seki village in Mino and Osafune village in Bizen.

Compared with Yamato people, they are somewhat smaller and more slender. Their skin is brown; besides black, their hair may be white, silver or gold. They are agile, particularly dexterous with their hands, excellent in endurance and surprisingly strong. But, perhaps from a lack of vitality, they are vulnerable to illness and short-lived.

Average life expectancy is thirty-odd years. Those who live more than fifty years are rare.

They also possess a peculiar ageless constitution. After reaching adulthood at around fifteen, their appearance changes very little until death.

The Yamato court histories first record them as the indigenous people of eastern Yamato. Even then, they are said to have possessed advanced smithing techniques, including the forging of armor. The accepted account traces the birth of Yamato smithing to contact with them.

Since the medieval period, there has been no technical gap between Yamato and Emishi smiths. Nevertheless, perhaps because of a difference in innate aptitude, Yamato work is generally inferior to Emishi work.

Thus, although subjected to the prejudice and contempt that accompany minority status, the Emishi have also been valued and respected as a community with precious skills, down to the present.

...According to one theory, their short life and agelessness arise precisely from their specialization as a smithing people. When mind, body and craft reach maturity, an Emishi is destined to make the self into plate. A stage of life called old age is therefore unnecessary, the theory says.

Several peoples outside Yamato are thought to be of the same kind. Western anthropology collectively calls them the 'dwarves'. One pale-skinned people is perhaps the best known.

Spread throughout Europe, they amassed immense wealth selling armor and other weapons. Called merchants of death and hidden masters of the world, they became objects of fear and hatred—and for that reason suffered the greatest calamity of the recent World War.

They are called the Yudea.
In Yamato: White Emishi.
ja:
蝦夷えみしとは大和の少数民族を指す。

　彼らは小規模の集団を作って全国各地に散在するが、
全般的に見れば東北地方に近付くほど集団の規模・数
ともに増大する。しかし他地方でも鍛冶の名地（美濃
の関せき村や備前の長船おさふね村など）には集中して住む。

　大和人と比べてやや小柄かつ細身の体格を持ち、肌
は褐色、髪色は黒のほか白、銀、金などがみられる。
　動きは俊敏で特に手先が器用であり、持久力に秀で、
意外なほど筋力もあるが……

　生命力を欠くのか、病には弱く短命である。
　平均寿命は三十数年程度、五〇年以上を生きる者は
珍しい。

　また彼らは特異な不老体質を備え、一五歳頃に成人
を迎えて以後は死ぬまでほとんど容姿が変化しない。

　東大和の先住民族として大和朝廷の歴史書に記述が
現れる当初から劔冑鍛造を始めとする高度な鍛冶技術
を有していたとされ、大和鍛冶の誕生は彼らとの接触
が端緒であると通説は認める。

　中世以降、大和鍛冶と蝦夷鍛冶の間に技術的な格差
はみられないが、種族的な適性の部分で差があるのか、
一般に大和鍛冶の作品は蝦夷鍛冶のそれに及ばない。

　そのため、蝦夷は少数民族の必然として偏見・蔑視
を受けつつも、貴重な職能集団と扱われ、尊重されて、
現在に至っている。

　……一説によれば、彼らの短命と不老は鍛冶種族と
して特化されているからこそだと云う。
　蝦夷は心身と技術の成熟を迎えた時点で己を甲鉄ヨロイと
するのが宿命。老境などという人生は必要ない、と。

　大和国外にも同類と考えられる種族は複数存在し、
西洋人類学はこれを総じて『小さい人ドワーフ』と呼称する。
　そのうち特に有名なものは白い肌の一種族であろう。

　彼らは欧州全域に分布し、劔冑を始めとする武器の
販売で巨富を築き、死の商人と、世界の黒幕と呼ばれ
畏怖と嫌悪を集め――それが為に、
　先の世界大戦においては最大の災厄を蒙こうむった。

　彼らを称して賛美者の末裔ユーデア。
　大和語では白蝦夷と云う。

en:
Dredging up textbook knowledge about the people in front of me would change nothing, and I knew it. A few things, however, I could nod at: Fuki's attitude, the house standing alone in the mountains, and, on the other hand, an air of not being particularly poor.

The whole complicated condition of the Emishi as a people could be found packed into this one small house. With a single exception. The child's cheerfulness.
ja:
……視界の中の人々にまつわる教科書的知識を引き
出したところで、何が変わるというものでもない。
　だがいくつか、頷けることはあった。ふきという娘
の態度、山中孤立の家、反面そう貧困でもない佇まい。

　蝦夷という種族の複雑な在り方はこの小さな家の中
にもすべて詰まっていると言えた。
　唯一、子供の快活さだけを例外として。

en:
ふな"Bhaiya, where did you come from?"

Kageaki"From the town of Kamakura."

ふな"Kamakura... I have never gone, but I know it. Big city, no?"

Kageaki"Yes. At present it is the de facto capital of Yamato."

ふな"De-fakto capital?"

Kageaki"A capital is the foremost city of a country. 'De facto' means, strictly it is not that, but in practice that is what it amounts to."

ふな"So Kamakura is like the number-one city?"

Kageaki"Yes."

ふな"Then where is the real capital?"

Kageaki"Kyoto, in Yamashiro no kuni. It can still be said to hold a central place in Kinki and farther west, but..."

Kageaki"Nearly all of western Yamato is still on a slow road of recovery from the war damage. Kyoto's bustle is only what that allows."

ふな"Kamakura is more amazing?"

Kageaki"There are a great many people."

ふな"How many?"

Kageaki"Twice this village. Then ten times. Then about a hundred times."

ふな"Kyaa! Wah, so amazing..."
ja:
ふな
「にーやはどこから来たの？」




景明
「鎌倉の町から参りました」




ふな
「かまくらー……。
　いったことないけど、しってる。でっかい
まち？」




景明
「はい。現在の大和における事実上の首都で
すから」




ふな
「じじつじょうのしゅと？」




景明
「首都とは、国で一番の都のことです。
　事実上とは、本当は違うのだけれども大体
そのようなものである、という意味です」




ふな
「かまくらは……いちばんのみやこみたいな
もの？」




景明
「はい」




ふな
「ほんとうのしゅとは？」




景明
「山城國やましろのくに、京都です。
　現在も近畿以西においては中心的な位置を
占めていると言えるのですが……」




景明
「しかし、大和西部は未だほぼ全域が遅々と
して進まぬ戦災からの復興の途上にあります。
　京都の賑わいも相応のものに過ぎません」




ふな
「かまくらはもっとすごい？」




景明
「人が大勢います」




ふな
「どのくらい？」




景明
「この村の倍の、十倍の、百倍ほど」




ふな
「きゃー！
　すごいねぇ……」

en:
The younger girl clapped her hands in excitement. Funa, was it? Since a while ago she had been stuck to me, the sudden intruder, and would not come off.

Not a child who feared things, evidently.
ja:
はしゃいで、ぱちぱちと手を叩く下の娘。
　ふなという名前だったか。先程から、突然の闖入者
である俺にくっついて離れない。

　物怖じしない性格のようだ。

en:
ふき"Funaa! Don't trouble the warrior sahib so much."

ふな"Nnn."

Kageaki"No, please do not worry. Lying here doing nothing is dull, so her company is a help, if anything."

ふな"I am not troubling!"

ふき"Uff... honestly."
ja:
ふき
「ふなー。
　あまりお武家様を困らせないの」




ふな
「んぅー」




景明
「いえ、お気遣いなく。
　ただ寝ているだけというのは無聊なもの、
かえって助かります」




ふな
「こまってない！」




ふき
「もぅ……」

en:
弥源太"Sorry for the trouble, Mido."

Kageaki"None at all."

弥源太"Who she takes after, I do not know. Not a grain of calm in her. In the daytime she plays outside, which is fine. After dark she has no work but disturbing us."

ふき"Haan, exactly! Let her into the kitchen, and into the pot her hand wants to go, she wants to touch Grandpa's knives, and when I look away the whole cupboard is turned out on the floor..."

ふき"I am sorry to say it, warrior sahib, but today you have saved me."
ja:
弥源太
「世話を掛けるな、御堂」




景明
「とんでもありません」




弥源太
「そやつは誰に似たやら、まるで落ち着きと
いうものがなくて困っておる。
　昼は外で遊んでおるから良いが、夜になる
とうてらの邪魔しかすることがないらしい」




ふき
「そうなんですよぅ。
　台所に来ればおなべに手を入れようとする
し、じっちゃまの刃物は触りたがるし、気が
つくと箪笥の中身をひっくり返してるし……」




ふき
「申しわけないですけど、今日はお武家様の
お陰で助かっちゃってます」

en:
The old man, polishing what looked like a carpenter's tool, and the older girl, standing in the kitchen, agreed in chorus. The youngest member of the house was clearly a bit of a hooligan.

When she jumped onto my stomach, in person, doubt ended.
ja:
大工道具かなにかと思しき刃物を磨いている老人と、
厨房に立っている上の娘が口を合わせる。
　この家の最年少者はなかなかの暴れん坊のようだ。
実際、腹の上に飛び乗って来られては疑うべくもない。

en:
ふき"...And right while I am saying it! You cannot do that to an injured person!"

Kageaki"Please do not mind."
ja:
ふき
「……って言ってるそばからもー！
　怪我してる人にそんなことしちゃ駄目！」




景明
「お気遣いなく」

en: ふき"I DO mind. Let me mind! Now behave, chup-chaap!"
ja:
ふき
「遣います遣わせてくださいっ！
　ほら、おとなしくしてる！」

en: ふな"Waaah."
ja:
ふな
「わー」

en: The older girl flew in from the kitchen, hoisted her sister up and moved her aside, then went straight back. She seemed to be in the middle of work she could not leave; everything was in a rush.
ja:
厨房から飛んでくるや、妹を担ぎ上げて脇へのけ、
また戻っていく上の娘。
　手が離せない仕事の最中らしく、慌しい。

en:
Muramasa《This house is noisier than I expected...》

Kageaki(The odd guest may be partly responsible. I do not think many visitors come to this house.)

Muramasa《True. ...Just a little, this air feels nostalgic.》

Kageaki(Is it similar?)

Muramasa《Who knows. I had no younger sister. But perhaps an Emishi house has an Emishi-house smell of its own.》

Kageaki(...I see. You are Emishi too. Now that it is said, of course.)

Muramasa《...Indeed, we had not even talked about that much. Should I have told you something?》

Kageaki(Do you think so?)

Muramasa《............No. And you? Do you want to hear?》

Kageaki(No.)

Muramasa《...Achha. Incidentally...》

Kageaki(What?)

Muramasa《That girl Fuki. Is there some deep reason behind the way she treats me?》

Kageaki(No. I believe she was simply in a hurry.)
ja:
村正
《意外に騒々しい家ね……》



景明
（珍客のせいでもあるだろう。
　あまり来訪者の多い家とは思えん）



村正
《そうね。
　……少しだけ、懐かしい。この空気》



景明
（似ているのか）



村正
《どうかしら。
　私に妹はいなかったし……けどやっぱり、
蝦夷の家には蝦夷の家の匂いがあるのかもし
れない》



景明
（……そうか。
　お前も蝦夷か。言われてみれば当然のこと
だな）



村正
《……そういえば、そんなことさえも話して
いなかったのね。
　少しは……話しておくべきだったのかしら》



景明
（そう思うのか）



村正
《…………いいえ。
　貴方は？　聞きたいと思う？》



景明
（いいや）



村正
《……そう。
　ところで……》



景明
（何だ）



村正
《あのふきっていう娘の、私に対する仕打ち
には何か底深い理由があるのかしら》



景明
（いや。
　単に慌てていただけだと思うが）

en: I offered this personal view to the armor now being sat upon by the younger sister. Muramasa looked faintly disgruntled; the girl looked delighted with her new toy.
ja:
そこはかとなく憮然たる様子で妹娘に座られて・・・・いる
劔冑に個人的見解を述べておく。
　玩具を与えられた格好の娘は、ご満悦のようだった。

en:
ふき"Dinner will be ready soon! Warrior sahib, please wait. Today I have put in my full effort."

Kageaki"Please do not trouble yourself."

弥源太"Putting in effort is fine. But have you remembered that it is food for an injured man?"

ふき"Of course. Ah, warrior sahib, is there anything you do not like?"

Kageaki"I am somewhat poor with heavily oily things. Otherwise nothing in particular."

ふき"Theek hai, good, no problem! Grandpa, please put out the dining table!"

弥源太"............"

ふき"Grandpa?"

弥源太"...Dinner will be a little later. A guest has come. The unwelcome kind."

Kageaki"!"

ふき"Eh...?"
ja:
ふき
「もうすぐごはんできますからねー。
　お武家様、待っててください。今日は腕に
よりをかけましたからっ」




景明
「どうかお構いなく」




弥源太
「腕をふるうのは良いがな。
　怪我人に食わす物だということはちゃんと
考えておるのか？」




ふき
「もちろん。
　あ、お武家様。好き嫌いはあります？」




景明
「油の強いものがやや苦手ですが、ほかには
別段」




ふき
「よしっ、大丈夫！
　じっちゃま、ちゃぶ台出しておいてー」




弥源太
「…………」




ふき
「じっちゃま？」




弥源太
「……飯は少し後だ。
　客が来たらしい。招かれざる類のな」




景明
「！」




ふき
「え……？」

en: 小太郎"Pardon the late hour. Only a small intrusion, only a little. Whatever the business, once it is done we shall be gone at once."
ja:
小太郎
「夜分に失礼。
　少々お邪魔致し申す。何、用を済ませたら
すぐに退散しますでの」

en: ふき"Wh-who... who are you people..."
ja:
ふき
「な、なっ、なんですかっ、あなたたち……」

en:
長坂"..."

ふき"! M-Magistrate sahib!?"
ja:
長坂
「……」



ふき
「！　お、お代官様!?」

en:
The young woman, who had managed to kick the door open and deliver a courteous greeting in one motion, was young in appearance only. Behind her, slowly, came an older man. The two who had to come had come.

But far sooner than I had expected! They were not unhurt either; I had judged they could not possibly arrive within this night. Evidently I had underestimated the ninja's ability.
ja:
戸を蹴り開ける非礼と慇懃な挨拶とを一緒にやって
のけた若い女――注釈、外見上。
　そして、その後ろからのっそりと現れる初老の男。

　来るべくして来た二人だった。

　しかし――予想より遥かに早い！　向こうとて無傷
ではなし、よもやこの夜の内に来ることはなかろうと
見込んでいた。
　乱破者の実力を甘く見たか……。

en:
Kageaki(Muramasa.)

Muramasa《No fighting! your body and my plate: neither can stand up to flight!》

Kageaki(Understood. Give me the tachi only.)

Muramasa《...Are you serious!?》

Kageaki(I am choosing the best move among limited means. It is not especially a joke.)

Muramasa《But...!》
ja:
景明
（村正）



村正
《戦闘は不可能！
　仕手あなたの肉体、騎体わたしの甲鉄、共に騎航に耐え
られる状態に無し！》



景明
（諒解した。
　太刀だけ寄越せ）



村正
《……本気!?》



景明
（限られた手段のうちから最善手を選択して
いるだけの事。格別、冗談じみてはおるまい）



村正
《けれど……！》

en: I checked behind the pair, and listened for sounds. There did not seem to be one more hiding anywhere nearby. Not that I could rule out a cleverly hidden one.
ja:
二人の背後と、物音を確認する。
　……もうひとり・・・・・、どこかに潜んでいるということは
無さそうだ。巧妙に隠れていないとは限らないが。

en:
小太郎"Ho-ho. Here he is, here he is, look, here. Now then..."

Kageaki"Wait. I will hear your business outside. There is no need to drag the people of this house into it."

小太郎"If you would do that, it saves us trouble as well."
ja:
小太郎
「ほっほ。おったおった、ほれおった。
　さぁて……」




景明
「待て。
　話は外で聞く。この家の人々を巻き込むに
は及ばん」




小太郎
「そうしてくれれば、こちらも助かるがの」

en:
I raised myself from the warm bedding. Pain ran through me, and blood seeped into the bandage. Had the wound opened a little?

But I was not unable to move.
ja:
温かだった寝床から身を起こす。
　苦痛が走る――包帯に血が滲む。少し傷口が開いた
か。

　しかし、動けなくはない。

en:
ふき"Warrior sahib! You must not!"

Kageaki"You have looked after me very well. A tedious errand has come up, so I will take my leave now. I shall come another day to thank you properly."

ふき"B-but—"

小太郎"Ha-ha! Another day, he says! Another day!"

Kageaki"That was not a place to laugh."

小太郎"It is, Kageaki Minato! No matter... that thanks-another-day, this old man will deliver on your behalf."

ふき"..."

Kageaki"Very well. Then as a gift, Tomoshimaya's Hato Sabure, the twelve-piece set. And one bottle of Yamakura Brewery's Kugyo. It should not cause you much trouble."

小太郎"Understood. I shall see to it exactly so."
ja:
ふき
「お武家様！　いけません！」




景明
「大変お世話になりました。
　少々つまらぬ用事が出来たようなのでこれ
にて失礼を。後日、改めて御礼に参上させて
頂きます」




ふき
「そ、そんな」




小太郎
「はっは！　後日、後日か！」




景明
「今のは別に笑う所ではないが」




小太郎
「笑う所だよ、湊斗景明。
　まあ良いわえ……後日の御礼とやらは儂が
代わりに済ませてやろうぞ」




ふき
「……」




景明
「そうか。なら手土産は友島屋の鳩サブレー、
一二枚セットで頼む。あと山倉醸造の『公暁』
を一瓶。
　おそらく造作を掛けることはなかろうが」




小太郎
「心得た。
　必ず、そのようにしてくれよう」

en:
Answering Kotaro Fuma's bared-teeth grin, I got to my feet.

They wobbled a little. Short of blood, perhaps? My calves had gone weak. But they moved. If they moved, I could fight. For fighting, nothing else is required.
ja:
風魔小太郎の歯を見せた笑いに応えて、足腰を立た
せる。
　……わずかに揺らいだ。血が足りないのか、脹脛ふくらはぎが
萎えている。

　だが動く。動けば、戦える。
　戦うためには、他に何も必須ではない。

en:
Kageaki"...Sorry to keep you waiting."

小太郎"Ho. No matter. An old man's patience is long. Shall we go, then?"
ja:
景明
「……待たせた」




小太郎
「ほっ。なに、構わぬよ。爺は気が長いでな。
　では参ろうか……」

en:
At his prompting, I went down to the earthen floor.

Or rather, I tried to. An arm shot out smoothly and blocked my way.
ja:
促されるまま、土間に降りる。

　否、降りようとした――が。
　ついと伸びた腕に、行く手を遮られた。

en:
弥源太"..."

Kageaki"Elder."

弥源太"Step back."

Kageaki"But this is my—"

弥源太"This is my house. Whom to receive as a guest and whom not to, that is for me to decide."

Kageaki"..."

弥源太"The Emishi have no custom of handing a guest over to ruffians. Such a thing is the greatest disgrace there is. Mido, unless you want to hang the name of shameless on this old man, leave it to me first."

Kageaki"............As you wish."
ja:
弥源太
「……」




景明
「御老」




弥源太
「下がられい」




景明
「しかし、これは自分の」




弥源太
「ここはうての家。
　誰を客として迎え、誰を迎えぬかはうてが
決めること」




景明
「……」




弥源太
「客人を狼藉者に引き渡すなどという作法を
蝦夷は持たん。かような真似こそ最大の恥辱。
　御堂、この爺に恥知らずの汚名を着せたく
思うのでなくば、まずは任せてもらおう」




景明
「…………御意に」

en:
Once it was called shame, there was nothing more to say. I drew back, for the time being.

If anything happened, however, I would have to cut in at once. I drew Muramasa to my hand, but only after carefully moving the small girl, silent and wide-eyed, deeper into the room. Sensing the strange atmosphere, Funa's eyes were wet.

...Bitterness gathered beneath my tongue.
ja:
恥辱と告げられては是非もなし。
　やむなく、ひとまず引き下がる。

　しかし事あらば即座に割り込まねばならない。
　村正は手元に引き寄せておいた。瞳を見開いて押し
黙っている小さな娘を慎重に部屋の奥へ移した後で。

　異様な雰囲気を感じ取ってだろう、ふなという娘の
目元は潤んでいた。
　……舌の裏側に苦渋が湧く。

en:
小太郎"Ho-ho. What a brave old gentleman. But they say that when a man ages, his bones rot. Better not to overexert."

弥源太"I am old, that is a fact, and there is no reason to be angry at hearing it. Still, I do object to having poison thrown at me by a freak like you. Watch your mouth."

小太郎"Ha-ha! Oh dear, oh dear. I, who know only slightly more of play than other people, am to be called a monster? Rather unfair."

小太郎"But master of the house, if you see me as a monster, then, since it is a special occasion, I am not unwilling to behave like one...?"

長坂"No need. Stand back."
ja:
小太郎
「ほぅ、ほぅ。これは勇ましき御老人かな。
　しかし、歳食えば骨朽ちると申す。無理は
慎まれたが宜しかろう」




弥源太
「……年寄っておるのは事実ゆえ、言われて
怒る筋はないがな。
　それでも貴様の如き化生けしょうに毒舌を叩かれる
のは心外というもの。その口こそ慎まれたい」




小太郎
「はっは！　これはしたり、これはしたり。
　人よりいささか遊び・・を知っておる程度の儂、
化生呼ばわりはちと心外なる申されよう」




小太郎
「だが家主殿。
　儂を化生と見られるならば、折角のこと、
そのように振舞わぬではないが……？」




長坂
「無用だ。
　控えておれ」

en: From behind the sorcerer licking his lips, the man who had stayed silent till now stepped forward and stood facing Elder Yagenta.
ja:
唇を舐めた、外法者の背後から。
　それまでは黙りこくっていた男が踏み出し、弥源太
老人との間に立ち塞がった。

en:
小太郎"Magistrate."

長坂"I will deal with this one. ...No complaint, Yagenta?"

弥源太"Complaint? These days my one complaint is that you and I are still clinging to this world at all, Ukyo Nagasaka."

長坂"Ha. Listen to him. There were countless chances to settle this, and who kept running away all this time? Bhagoda."

弥源太"No need to remind me. That is why I call it a complaint. Why could I not decide sooner...?"

長坂"Even that regret comes thirty years late! If you had not run then, one of us would have got something out of life, and the other at least would have been spared this show of decrepitude!"
ja:
小太郎
「代官殿」




長坂
「こやつの相手は俺がする。
　……不満はなかろう？　弥源太」




弥源太
「不満か。今となっては、なれとうてが現世うつしよ
にいつまでもしがみついておる事こそ不満で
ならぬよ。
　長坂右京……」




長坂
「は。抜かすわ。
　けりをつける機会ならいくらでもあったに、
逃げ続けてきたのは何処の誰ぞ？」




弥源太
「言われるまでもない。
　だから不満と言うておる。なぜもっと早く、
決断ができなんだか……」




長坂
「その後悔さえ、三十年遅いわ！
　あの時に貴様が逃げなければ、我らの一方
は人生に実りを得、もう一方とて少なくとも
老廃を晒さずには済んだであろうよ」

en:
The gazes of the two old men collided head-on. A curtain of silence fell.

Nobody spoke, nobody moved. While those two stood still, nobody else could move either. The magistrate's words, thirty years, seemed to have turned solid and packed every corner of the room.

I could not step in. My hands and feet felt tied. Even breathing was hard.
ja:
二人の老いた男の視線が正面から相撃つ。
　沈黙の帳が下りた。

　誰も、何も口にしない。身動きもしない。
　あの二人が不動なら、他には誰も動けない。

　代官の口にした三十年という言葉が、固形と化して
空間の隅々まで詰まったかのようだった。
　――立ち入れない。手足が縛られている。息苦しさ
さえ覚える。

en:
弥源太"...I do not think this life of mine bore no fruit."

長坂"I do. I got nothing. Nothing at all."

弥源太"..."

長坂"Deep down you think the same. Or will you insist those granddaughters have satisfied you?"

弥源太"Is there a reason I must not say so?"

長坂"Because that is not what you sought."

弥源太"What one seeks, one does not always get, and what one gets instead is not worth less for that. I say my life existed to send these children into the world, and I do not mind saying it."

長坂"...I see. If that is your declaration, then keep it. Then why challenge me now?"

弥源太"So that I do not drag regret into the land of the dead. Your folly, either Ichihime or I had to stop. With Ichihime gone, only I am left."

弥源太"If I die leaving my duty undone, I will lose my way on the road to Yomi. Ukyo, carving your epitaph will be my last work."

長坂"Then my work is carving yours? Hmph. Troublesome."

長坂"I will feed you to the dogs and be done with it. No objection?"

弥源太"Good!"
ja:
弥源太
「……うてはこの一命に実りがなかったとは
思うておらぬ」




長坂
「俺は思っておるよ。
　何も得られなんだわ……何もな」




弥源太
「……」




長坂
「貴様とて本心ではそうであろう。
　それともその孫娘どもを得て満足だとでも
言い張るつもりか？」




弥源太
「そう言ってはならぬ理由があるか？」




長坂
「貴様が求めたのはそれ・・ではなかろう」




弥源太
「求めたものを得られるとは限らぬし、そう
でないものの価値がそれより劣るとも言えぬ。
　うての命はこやつらを世に送り出すために
あったと、そう言うても一向に構わぬ」




長坂
「……そうか。貴様がそう言うならそれでも
良かろうさ。
　ならば貴様は何故、今になって俺に挑む？」




弥源太
「冥途へ悔いを引き摺らぬ為よ。
　なれの馬鹿はうてか一媛いちひめが止めねばならな
かった。一媛亡き今はうてしかおらぬ」

弥源太
「己の責務を残して逝けば黄泉路に迷うわ。
　右京、なれの墓碑銘を刻むことが、うての
最後の仕事となろうよ」




長坂
「では俺の仕事は貴様の墓碑を刻むことか？
　ふん、厄介な」




長坂
「犬に食わせて済ます。構うまい？」




弥源太
「良かろうよ！」

en:
The old man tore something from the top of the simple shrine on the wall. The magistrate dropped the armor chest from his back onto the earthen floor.

What Elder Yagenta held was a short rod. That... some kind of fang?

The magistrate kicked the chest lid roughly open and set both fists before his chest: the Soukou no kamae, according to naval regulations!
ja:
老人は、壁の素朴な神棚の上から何かをもぎ取った。
　代官は背負っていた鎧櫃を土間へ落とす。

　弥源太老人が手にしたのは短い棒状の物。
　あれは――何かの牙か？

　鎧櫃の蓋を乱暴に蹴り開け、代官が両拳を胸の前で
構える。
　――海軍礼則に法のっとる装甲ノ構ソウコウノカマエ！

en: 長坂"Yagenta..."
ja:
長坂
「弥源太……」

en: 弥源太"Ukyo...!"
ja:
弥源太
「右京……！」

en:
Kanae"Thank goodness. I was worried they might mistake it for the starting signal."

Sayo"Be at ease, Miss. Nobody said 'on your marks, get set.'"
ja:
香奈枝
「良かった。
　もしスタートの合図と勘違いされたらどう
しようかと思ってました」

さよ
「大丈夫ですよ、お嬢さま。
『位置について用意』とは誰も言っておりま
せんでしたから」

en:
...A sudden gunshot. What followed it was this kind of chatter.

Without any visible wariness, two figures came in through the open doorway. Both women: one young and tall, the other old and small.

Following exactly behind the long-haired, young-lady type was the white-haired attendant, who surveyed the room and frowned.
ja:
……やにわの銃声。
　続けて聞こえてきたのは、そんな話し声だった。

　特に警戒した様子もなく、人影が二つ、開き放しの
戸口から入り込んでくる。
　いずれも女性。一方は若く長身、もう一方は老いて
小柄。

　長髪をなびかせる令嬢風の女性にぴたりと付き従う
白髪の侍従は、室内を見回すや、ふと眉をひそめた。

en: Sayo"...What is this old-people-smelling space?"
ja:
[text0310a]

さよ
「……なんですか、この年寄り臭い空間は」

en:
Kanae"Nanny, you are the last person to say that."

長坂"You are..."

Kageaki"Inspector."

Kanae"Thank goodness, Mr. Minato. So you were here. I was worried, you know? You went out saying you would investigate, you did not return even after dark, and not one word of contact."

Kageaki"That was a serious lapse on my part. I met with some difficulty and had no time to contact you. I deeply apologize for the needless worry."

Sayo"Arre, arre, that injury... this was not needless at all. A well-founded worry, I see! How is your condition?"

Kageaki"Embarrassing. A wound from my own carelessness. It was not shallow, but thanks to the people here I am out of danger. Please do not trouble yourselves."

Sayo"Is that so. That is a relief, Miss."

Kanae"Yes. Truly, I am glad you are safe. Mr. Minato is my dear benefactor. If these people helped him, I must thank them as well."

Kanae"Thank you very much."

ふき"Eh? Yes... n-no, it is nothing—"
ja:
[text0310b]

香奈枝
「ばあや、あなたが言わないの」




長坂
「貴様は……」




景明
「巡察官殿」




香奈枝
「良かった、湊斗さま。こちらにいらしたの
ですね。心配しておりましたのよ？
　捜査に行くと出ていかれたきり、日が暮れ
ても戻られないし、連絡一つないのですもの」




景明
「これは……とんだ不手際を。
　いささか難儀しておりまして、ご連絡する
暇いとまがありませんでした。いらぬ心労をお掛け
した事、深くお詫び致します」




さよ
「や、や、そのお怪我は……
　これはいらぬどころか妥当な心配であった
ご様子！　お加減はいかがなものでございま
しょう？」




景明
「お恥ずかしい。不覚傷です。
　浅からぬ負傷ではありましたが、こちらの
方々のお陰をもって大事なく済んでおります。
　どうかお気遣いなさいませぬよう」




さよ
「さようでございますか。
　よろしゅうございましたね、お嬢さま」




香奈枝
「ええ。本当に、ご無事で何より。

　それ以外の面で釣り合わない部分が多過ぎるが……。

en:
Sayo"That is the face of a man who is not at all displeased, Miss."

Kanae"My heart goes dhak-dhak."
ja:
さよ
「あれは満更でもないという顔でございます
よ、お嬢さま」




香奈枝
「どきどき」

en:
A man with my rough appearance beside someone so plainly a sheltered young lady would look out of place.
In manner and presentation, would Ichijou Ayane not be closer to my sort?

...A rude assessment, admittedly.
I could hardly say that to her face.
ja:
俺のような男の横に、いかにも深窓の令嬢然とした
女性を置いても釣り合いは取れないだろう。

　それならむしろ、あの綾弥一条の方が似合わないだ
ろうか？

　……なんだか、失礼な評価ではあるが。
　本人にはとても言えない。

en:
Sayo"Hm. That is the face of a man thinking about somebody else, Miss."

Kanae"Oh! How rude."
ja:
さよ
「む。あれは別の女性のことを考えている顔
ですよ、お嬢さま」




香奈枝
「まっ。なんて憎たらしい」

en:
...At most, Muramasa was what suited me.

Cold steel.
Iron the color of blood.
The shape of a crawling insect.
Neither warmth nor softness. Only a blade.

That was my proper station.
ja:
……俺に似合うのはせいぜい村正だろう。

　冷たい鋼。
　血の色の鉄。
　地べたを這い回る虫の形。
　温もりも柔らかさもない、ただの刃。

　それが――俺には分相応だ。

en: Muramasa《...》

Night deepened.

After dinner, Kanae took out the instrument she had brought and began to play. Since our first meeting I had been wondering what the gigantic case she never let out of her reach could possibly hold. When the lid finally came open, the answer arrived with no ceremony at all. It was a double bass. Just that.

Why an occupation-force officer should walk around with a double bass, I could not say. Perhaps I should not even be asking. This was a woman who traveled with an attendant at her heels, so ordinary reasons were presumably not on offer.

She broke convention in everything, it seemed. The double bass was only the largest piece of evidence.
ja:
……夜が更ける。

　食事が済むと、香奈枝は持参の楽器を奏で始めた。
　……最初に出会った時から、肌身離さぬあの巨大な
楽器ケースは一体何なのか疑問だったが、蓋を開けて
みれば答は呆気なく。そのまま、コントラバスだった。

　進駐軍士官がなぜそんなものを持ち歩いているのか。
　不思議がるべきではないのかもしれない。なにしろ
侍従を連れているような女性だ。

　何かにつけ型破りなのだろう。

en:
Muramasa《……?》

Kageaki"A good sound."

ふき"Sach mein..."

ふな"Fuwaaa..."

弥源太"..."
ja:
村正
《……？》



景明
「良い音です」




ふき
「本当に……」




ふな
「ふわー……」




弥源太
「……」

en:
An enemy of no small strength waited outside, and my body carried a wound of no small weight.

Even so, the hour was warm and gentle. For a moment I came close to remembering something that must not be remembered.

A scene far away, which I must not recall. A reality close at hand, which I must not forget: the fight still to come.

So, now, rest. Not to sink into comfort. For tomorrow's battle.

Now—sleep.
ja:
外には容易ならぬ敵がおり、
　身には軽からぬ傷。

　しかし、温かく和やかな一時。
　……ふと、思い出してはならぬものを思い出しそう
になる。

　思い出してはならない――遠い光景。
　忘れてはならない――戦うべき現実。

　今は休む。
　
　しかし、それは安らぎに浸るためでなく。
　明日の戦いのために。

　今は、
　眠る――――

en:
ふな"Hoi!"

Kageaki"Hah."
ja:
ふな
「ほいっ」




景明
「はっ」

en:
ふな"Hoi!"

Kageaki"Hah."
ja:
ふな
「ほいっ」




景明
「はっ」

en: Funa set a piece of firewood on the block. I dropped the heavy edge of the hatchet on it and split it. She pushed the halves aside and set down the next log.
ja:
ふなが台の上に置いてくれる薪へ、鉈の重い刃先を
落として割る。
　ふなはそれを脇へのかせ、再び薪を置く。

en:
ふな"Hoi!"

Kageaki"Hah."
ja:
ふな
「ほいっ」



景明
「はっ」

en:
ふき"Sorry, warrior sahib... making an injured guest chop wood like this."

Kageaki"I asked for it myself. Please do not worry. Light movement of this kind is good rehabilitation for me."

ふき"If you say so... But isn't it tiring? Whenever I chop wood, next day every muscle is aching, no?"

Kageaki"That is because you swing the hatchet with the strength of your arms."
ja:
ふき
「すいません、お武家様……。
　薪割りなんかさせちゃって」




景明
「自分の方よりお願いしたこと、どうかお気
になさらず。
　こうして軽く体を動かすのは良い慣らしリハビリに
なるのです」




ふき
「ならいいんですけど……
　大変じゃありません？　あて、薪割りする
と必ず次の日は筋肉痛になっちゃいますよ」




景明
「それは腕の力で鉈を振るおうとするからで
しょう」

en:
ふき"And warrior sahib does not?"

Kageaki"No. Take the strength out of the arms, like this—"
ja:
ふき
「お武家様は違うんですか？」




景明
「はい。
　このように、腕の力は抜き」

en:
Kageaki"—and let the hatchet's weight fall without interference. That alone is enough to split the wood."

ふき"Oh..."

Kageaki"It is not difficult. Push a heavy hatchet with arm strength and you will injure the tendons. This way is better."

Kageaki"If it is no trouble, I can show you properly later."

ふき"O-oh. Then... perhaps I will ask you to."
ja:
景明
「……鉈の重さをそのまま・・・・落とします。
　これで充分、割ることができます」




ふき
「はー……」




景明
「難しいことではありません。
　腕の力で重い鉈を扱えば、筋を痛めます。
このようにやられた方がよろしいでしょう」




景明
「ご迷惑でなければ後程お教えします」




ふき
「そ、そうですか。
　お願いしちゃおうかな……」

en:
Fuki went on with the washing beside me, looking a little dreamy about something. I went on splitting wood.

We had already made enough for the next several days. A larger stock would still do no harm.

Elder Yagenta was working inside the house. Mending one part or another seemed to be his morning routine. Ootori and her attendant were not here; they had gone back to the village during the night.

'We shall have to devise some method.'

Kanae's parting words crossed my mind on their own. With matters standing as they did, the magistrate's side would surely work on GHQ while buying itself time. That was the move to expect.

If they were allowed to, the village would not be saved. And my own objective would probably go unreached as well. Move at that leisurely pace and the time would arrive.

We needed a plan to pull out the enemy hiding in the sea of trees. I kept splitting wood and kept thinking.
ja:
どこかぽやっとした様子になって洗濯を続けるふき
の横で、こちらも薪割りを続行する。
　既にここ数日分の需要は満たしていた。しかしもう
少し、ストックを増やしておいてもいいだろう。

　弥源太老人は家の中で仕事をしている。朝方は家の
各所の修繕をするのが日課のようだ。
　大鳥主従はいない。昨夜のうちに村へ戻っていた。

　――何かしら、手立てを考えなくてはなりませんね。

　帰りがけ、香奈枝の残していった言葉がふと脳裏を
過よぎる。
　そう。事がこうなった以上、代官らはＧＨＱに働き
かけつつ時間を稼ぐ戦術に出る筈。

　それを許しては村は救われない。
　そしておそらく、俺の目的も達せられない。そんな
悠長にしていれば時間・・が来る。

　……樹海に潜む敵を引っ張り出す策が必要だ。
　思案を巡らせつつ、俺は薪を割った。

en:
Muramasa《You seem to be in good form...》

Kageaki(Yes. The wound has closed. I am somewhat short of blood, but I should manage.)

Kageaki(All that remains is to bring the body's movement back. And you?)

Muramasa《Damage to the plate is fully restored. For me too, only the adjustment of internal functions remains.》

Kageaki(Understood.)

Muramasa《............》

Kageaki(...? What is it?)
ja:
村正
《調子は悪くないようね……》



景明
（ああ。傷口は塞がった。少々血が足りんが
……何とかなるだろう）



景明
（後は体の動きを戻していくだけだ。
　お前は？）



村正
《甲鉄の損傷は復元完了。
　こちらも後は内部機能の調整だけね》



景明
（承知した）



村正
《…………》



景明
（……？　どうした）

en: I could feel her silence. An odd way to put it, but accurate. The line had not been cut. It was the presence of someone clamping her mouth shut, and it reached me somewhere in the brain that was joined to the armor.
ja:
沈黙が伝わってくる――というのも妙な話だが。
　通信を断ったのとは違う、押し黙る気配が、劔冑と
連結する脳髄のどこかに届いていた。

en:
Muramasa《...I had been wanting you to blame me.》

Kageaki(Blame you?)

Muramasa《You have not forgotten. Yesterday's lapse.》
ja:
村正
《……責めて欲しいと、思っていたのよ》



景明
（責める……？）



村正
《忘れたわけではないでしょう。
　昨日の不覚》

en:
Kageaki(Of course not.)

Muramasa《I neglected the search. When I noticed, the enemy was already in front of us... I doubt any armor in history has made such a spectacle of itself.》

Kageaki(Had I foreseen a new enemy coming, I would have ordered a sweep of the surroundings, and that would have been the end of it. I did not foresee it.)

Kageaki(The disgrace is mine, not yours.)

Muramasa《No. The pilot's duty is to cut down the enemy in front of him. The armor's duty is to assist. That is how a warrior's work is divided. Watching the surroundings is simply what an armor must do.》

Kageaki(............)

Muramasa《And that simple duty I neglected... If Mother or Grandfather came to know, how they would grieve. And I do not even know how to apologize to you.》
ja:
景明
（無論だ）



村正
《探査を怠り、気付いた時には敵は目前……。
　これほどの醜態を晒した劔冑もかつてない
でしょうね》



景明
（新手の襲来を予測していたなら、俺は周辺
の探査を命じた。それで済んだ。
　だが、俺はその予測ができなかった）



景明
（醜態を晒したのはお前ではなく、俺だ）



村正
《違う。仕手は目前の敵を打ち倒すのが務め。
劔冑の務めはその補佐。武者の役割分担とは
そういうものでしょう。
　周辺の警戒なんて劔冑として当然の義務よ》



景明
（…………）



村正
《その当然の義務を、私は怠った……。二世かかさま
や始祖じじさまが知ったらどれほど嘆くか。
　貴方にもどう詫びたらいいのかわからない》

en:
Her metal-echo shook as it reached me. Humiliation and anger, all of it aimed at herself.

I understood. So that was the matter. However—
ja:
届く金打声は震えを伴っていた。
　屈辱と、怒りの。すべて自分自身に向けられている。

　……成程。
　そういうことか。しかし。

en:
Kageaki(No apology is needed. Do not get this wrong, armor.)

Muramasa《...Mido?》

Kageaki(You had no role to begin with. No duty, no obligation. You are only a blade.)

Kageaki(Only a tool.)

Muramasa《............》

Kageaki(As pilot, using the armor properly is my duty. For the armor, being used is enough. Last evening I failed to use you. My duty I failed to perform. Therefore the failure's responsibility is mine.)

Kageaki(Understand? Duty, right, responsibility—all of it belongs to me alone. You have nothing. Naturally. No master pushes responsibility onto a slave.)

Muramasa《............》

Kageaki(Throw away this pointless brooding. Just keep sharpening your own edge.)

Muramasa《...I see. If that is what you say... then let us leave it there.》
ja:
景明
（詫びなどいらん。
　勘違いをするな、劔冑）



村正
《……御堂？》



景明
（お前に役割など端から無い。
　義務も務めもない。お前は只の刃）



景明
（只の道具だ・・・・・）



村正
《…………》



景明
（俺には仕手として劔冑を使いこなす義務が
ある。劔冑は使われていればそれでいい。
　昨夕の俺はお前を使い損ねた。義務を果た
さなかった。故に失敗の責任は俺にある）

景明
（わかるか？　義務にせよ権利にせよ責任に
せよ、全て俺一人の物だ。お前には何もない・・・・・・・・。
　当然だろう。奴隷に責任を押し付ける主人
などおらん）



村正
《…………》



景明
（愚にもつかぬ思案は捨てろ。
　お前はただ、己の刃を砥いでいればいい）



村正
《……そう。
　貴方がそう言うのなら……そうしておきま
しょう》

en:
The hard voice that had been ringing in my head fell silent. I brought my attention back to my eyes, and found that the stack of firewood had grown to a considerable size.

Only three people lived here. This much would keep their fires lit for some time.

Funa stood holding the next log, looking up at me as if to ask a question. I nodded.
ja:
脳内に打ち響く硬質の声が絶える。
　意識を視界へ戻す――ふと見れば、積み上げられた
薪は随分な量に達していた。

　わずか三人の暮らし、これだけあれば当分炊きつけ
に困ることはないだろう。
　次の薪を抱えて問うように見上げてくる幼い視線へ、
頷きを返す。

en:
Kageaki"That is enough for now."

ふな"We chopped sooo much!"

Kageaki"Yes. Thank you for your help."
ja:
景明
「このくらいにしましょう」




ふな
「いっぱいわった！」




景明
「はい。
　お手伝い、ありがとうございました」

en: As I said this and bowed, a dull creak sounded and the door of the house opened.
ja:
そう告げて、一礼をした時。
　鈍い軋きしみ音がして、家の戸口が開いた。

en:
弥源太"Mido. ...That is quite a lot of wood."

Kageaki"The young lady helped me. It was finished quickly."

ふな"I helped!"

弥源太"So you did. Shabaash. ...Mido, can I leave you in charge of the house for a while?"

Kageaki"Are you going out somewhere?"

弥源太"Yes. Down to the foothills. I should be back before noon."

Kageaki"Understood. I will keep the house."

弥源太"Sorry to ask. I leave it to you."
ja:
弥源太
「御堂。
　……これはまた、結構な量を」




景明
「御令嬢にお手伝い頂いたので。
　手早く片付いてしまいました」




ふな
「てつだったー！」




弥源太
「そうか。よくやったな。
　……それで御堂。少し留守を頼んでも良い
かな」




景明
「どちらかへお出掛けですか」




弥源太
「うむ。ちと麓まで下りてくる。
　昼までには戻れるだろう」




景明
「承知致しました。
　留守をお預かりします」




弥源太
「すまんな。
　よろしく頼む」

en:
The old man went down the mountain path with steady steps. A small cloth bundle was tucked under one arm.

Something white stuck out of its edge. White. A flower.

Visiting a grave? Rather late for the higan-e, though...
ja:
危なげのない足取りで、山道を下りてゆく老人。
　脇に少々の手荷物を抱えていた。小さな風呂敷包み。

　その端から何か、白いものが突き出している。
　白い――花。

　墓参りだろうか？
　彼岸会ひがんえにはいささか遅過ぎるが……。

en:

अत्रेममात्मानं प्रेषयामि प्रत्यर्पयामि च।
तमध्वनि परिगृह्णन्तु। सुखशतं कल्याणसहस्रं च तस्मै प्रयच्छन्तु।
पञ्चानां दिशां परिवर्तनगुणाः सह भवन्तु।
हे महाभाग्यधातुदेव। हे महानुग्रहधातुदेव। उत्तरचमसस्याष्टस्वलिन्देषु तिष्ठतम्।
yuvayor guṇam anugrahaṃ च दिवि भूमौ च प्रयच्छतम्।
विचित्रैकधातुहृदयम्। सर्वैकधातुप्रभा। दिग्रक्षकधातुचक्रम्। दिग्घातकधातुकरतलम्……

चतुर्णां धातूनामधिपतीनावाहयामि प्रार्थये च।
अत्रेममात्मानं प्रेषयामि प्रत्यर्पयामि च।

पञ्चानां दिशां परिवर्तनगुणाः सह भवन्तु।

युवयोर्गुणमनुग्रहं च दिवि भूमौ च प्रयच्छतम्।
विचित्रैकधातुहृदयम्। सर्वैकधातुप्रभा। दिग्रक्षकधातुचक्रम्। दिग्घातकधातुकरतलम्……

चतुर्णां धातूनामधिपतीनावाहयामि प्रार्थये च।
अत्रेममात्मानं प्रेषयामि प्रत्यर्पयामि च।
तमध्वनि परिगृह्णन्तु। सुखशतं कल्याणसहस्रं च तस्मै प्रयच्छन्तु।
पञ्चानां दिशां परिवर्तनगुणाः सह भवन्तु।

युवयोर्गुणमनुग्रहं च दिवि भूमौ च प्रयच्छतम्।
विचित्रैकधातुहृदयम्। सर्वैकधातुप्रभा। दिग्रक्षकधातुचक्रम्। दिग्घातकधातुकरतलम्……
ja:
――四金しこんの司を招き願い奉る。

　ここに御霊送り御返し候えば遊行の道にこれを拾い
百幸千福授け給え。五方化徳共々に在れ。

　大幸金神、大恵金神、願わくば北斗八廊に留まり、
御徳御恵おんとくおめぐみ、天上天下へ下し給え。

　奇一金心、全一金光、護方金輪、殺方金掌……

en:
The old Emishi kept reciting a scripture that would have made any knowledgeable listener tilt his head. Short phrases, again and again, again and again.

A shadow fell across him from behind, and still his voice did not stop. The string of words, aimed at something not human, went on. The man who had come up behind him made no move to cut it off.

Dozens of rounds, no, perhaps a hundred. When the old man's chant finally ceased, the man behind him opened his mouth, without hurry.
ja:
聞く人間が聞けば首を傾げたかもしれない経文を、
蝦夷の老人は延々と唱える。
　短い文言を繰り返し、繰り返し。


　背後からついと影が差した時も、声が途絶えること
はなかった。
　人ならぬものに向けられた言葉の羅列は続く。背後
に立った者も、あえて止めようとはしない。

　数十度、いや、百度も繰り返したろうか。
　ようやく老人の詠唱が止んだ時、背後に立った男は
おもむろに口を開いた。

en:
長坂"...Konjin liturgy? In a Pure Land temple, this is what you are chanting? The priest says nothing?"

弥源太"Gods and Buddhas who save people make no distinctions, he says. Besides, I know no other prayer."
ja:
長坂
「……金神祭詞か？
　浄土宗の寺で唱うようなものでもあるまい
に。和尚は何も言わんのか」




弥源太
「人を救う神仏に分け隔てはない……とよ。
　それに、うては他の祈りを知らん」

en: The old man showed no surprise at meeting the one he had crossed blades with last night. Meeting him here today was a different matter from last night's meeting. Surprise and trembling had no place in it.
ja:
昨夜、刃を突きつけ合った男と邂逅して、老人の顔
に驚きの色はない。
　今日、この場で会うことと、昨夜の出会いとは意味
が違う。驚きも戦慄おののきもここでは不要。

en:
弥源太"I have kept doing it ever since Ichihime came back here."

長坂"...Hmph. Come to think of it, it suits her. She is Konjin's bride, after all."
ja:
弥源太
「一媛がここへ帰ってきてから、ずっとそう
しておる」




長坂
「……ふん。
　考えてみれば、あやつにはふさわしいか。
何しろ金神の花嫁だからな」

en:
A smile with bitterness in it. The old man let out a bitter smile of his own.

That one remark was a key, and it opened the door to the past.
ja:
苦いものを含んだ笑み。
　老人も苦笑をこぼした。

　男の一言は過去の扉を開く鍵。

en:
Long ago, they had been a young man and a young Emishi.

To anyone watching, they must have been a ridiculous pair. From the very first meeting each regarded the other almost as the killer of his father. They fought over every excuse that came along, and more than once wounded each other badly enough to risk a life.

And still neither kept away from the other. Besides the young Emishi, the young man, whose edges were far too sharp, had exactly one other person in the village willing to keep his company. Besides the young man, the Emishi had exactly one other person who chose to associate with him.

That one person was Ichihime, a beautiful girl of their own age.

As the man and the Emishi came through adolescence, they understood what the girl's beauty really meant, and before long each decided that it had to be for himself.

Then, in due course, each learned that he was not the only one who had decided so.

At twenty, they drank together and promised a last contest to settle their long quarrel.

But the next morning, three people came to the appointed ground. To the two young men, staring, she, Ichihime, announced:

'Ahaha! So I become the bride of the stronger one? But however strong you two are, you cannot beat Konjin of the mountain, can you? Then it can't be helped. I'll go and marry the god instead.'

The young Emishi was ashamed of himself and went back to the mountain. The young man would not give up. He kept demanding a contest from the Emishi and marriage from the girl, and neither would agree.

When the girl left the village, the young man too, soon after, was gone.
ja:
――遠い昔。
　彼らは若い男と、若い蝦夷だった。

　傍目にはいかにもおかしな二人であったろう。
　彼らは出会いの最初から互いを親の仇のように強く
意識し、あらゆる契機をとらえては争い、命に関わる
怪我を負わせ合うことさえ一再ではなく、

　それでいて、互いに遠ざけ合うことがなかった。
　圭角が強過ぎる若い男と付き合う村人は若い蝦夷の
ほかにはもう一人だけであり、蝦夷と好んで関わろう
とする者も若い男のほかには一人だけだった。

　そのもうひとりが一媛いちひめ。
　二人と同じ年頃の、美しい娘だった。

　男と蝦夷は思春期を経て、娘の美しさの本当の意味
に気がつき、ほどなく、それは自分のためでなくては
ならないと考えるようになる。

　そして、そう考える者が己だけではなく、もう一人
いることもやがて知った。
　二十歳を数えたある日、二人は長年の争いに決着を
つけるべく、最後の勝負を約して杯を交わした。

　しかし、翌朝。
　決闘の場に現れたのは三人。
　目を瞠みはる若者二人に、彼女、一媛は告げたのだった。

『あはは！　そうか、あたしは強い方の嫁になるのか。
　でもおまえ達がどれほど強くても、お山のこんじん
さまには勝てないだろうな？　それじゃあ仕方がない。
　あたしは神様のもとへ嫁に行くことにするよ』

　若い蝦夷は己を恥じ、山へ帰った。
　若い男は諦めず、なおも蝦夷に勝負を、娘に結婚を
求めたが、どちらも応じることはなく。
　娘が村を去ると、やがて男も姿を消した。

en: That was the whole story. Thirty years ago, in this village, such a thing had happened.
ja:
……それだけの話。
　三十年前のこの村で、そんな出来事があった。

en:
長坂"That woman... did she ever marry?"

弥源太"It seems not. After leaving the village she lived with her elder brother and his wife in Sunpu, I hear."

長坂"Hm?"

弥源太"Some seven years ago that household failed in its duties and was ruined, so she moved to Kamakura, taking in the orphaned child of her nephew and his wife along the way. All of this is secondhand, from the priest."

長坂"And after that?"

弥源太"She came back to the village three years ago. As white bones. Apparently she had left word to bury her here."

長坂"...That woman. Did she truly do as that nonsense said? Died unmarried, had herself buried here where she could look at the mountain..."

弥源太"Who knows. I don't."

長坂"..."

弥源太"But Ukyo. I wonder whether you ever took it for nonsense in the first place."

長坂"What do you mean?"

弥源太"Why dig into the mountain?"

長坂"..."

弥源太"Is it money you want?"

長坂"Having money causes trouble to whom?"

弥源太"Then there are plenty of other ways to build up industry. You need not play the prospector on the strength of one dubious legend."

長坂"..."

弥源太"Ichihime is gone."

長坂"She remains."

弥源太"Ukyo..."

長坂"The mountain's god of calamity—she said she would marry him. Kill that god, and Ichihime comes into my hands. That is the reasoning."

弥源太"............"

長坂"God's ore vein is there? I take it. Nothing there? I spit and laugh. Either is fine. Either way, mine is the victory."

弥源太"...So that is what you have in mind. Nothing has changed since the old days. You are a fool, Ukyo."

長坂"I have changed. Back then I could not admit my own stupidity, and I put on a useless show of dignity. Not now."

長坂"Any form will do. I will have her. Having her is enough, whether as a corpse or without even a corpse."

長坂"By whatever means. Neither the god nor you will obstruct me."

弥源太"...Foolish."

長坂"Yes. Foolish."

　何も無いなら唾を吐いて嗤う。

弥源太
「……やはり、そういう存念か。
　昔と何も変わらん。愚かな男だ、なれは」

「変わったさ。昔は己の愚劣ぶりを認められ
なかったからな。いらぬ格好をつけていた。
　今は違う」

長坂
「どのような形でもいい。
　俺はあやつを手に入れる。手に入ればそれ

長坂

en:
A breeze stirred, gentle and soft, passing through the gap between them. Yet it also divided them, as a great river divides its two banks.

Words no longer reached the far shore. Only their eyes crossed.
ja:

　緩やかな風。二人の隙間をやわらかく抜けてゆく、
それはしかし、大河のように両岸を隔ててもいる。

　もはや対岸に言葉は届かず、ただ視線を交わすのみ。

en:
長坂"Well, then..."

弥源太"You are leaving?"

長坂"Thanks to present circumstances, I am in no position to enjoy a leisurely stroll. Still, this will be settled in a day or two."

弥源太"Before then, the crimson warrior will come to kill you."

長坂"Then he will be killed in return."

弥源太"...Ukyo."

長坂"What?"

弥源太"The god of calamity may already have descended."

長坂"............What?"

弥源太"If so, even your doings are empty."

弥源太"Stop hiding, Ukyo. Come straight to me, now. I will face you. If calamity cannot be avoided, I would at least cut down the seeds of regret."

長坂"...Senile nonsense. I wondered what you meant to say."

長坂"Is that meant as provocation, Yagenta? Naturally you would like to settle this while that detestable girl is about. I prefer the reverse. Once she has been driven off, I shall deal with you properly."

弥源太"..."

長坂"Wait for it. That head, I will certainly—"

弥源太
「……右京」

弥源太

弥源太

　災厄が避けられぬものならせめて、悔いの

弥源太
「……」




長坂
「待っておれ。

en:
Seeing the figure that had appeared, both old men forgot themselves.

A girl, in a school uniform that ought to have been out of place here, though it oddly suited her.

She looked from one to the other with suspicion. Their faces plainly meant nothing to her.

For the two men it was different. Their mouths shaped the same word at the same moment, without a sound.

Ichihime.

The girl lost patience with the pair of them standing rooted there. She twisted her lip and spoke in the voice kept for obvious frauds.
ja:
その、現れた人影を見て。
　二人の老人は愕然と、我を忘れた。

　少女だった。
　学生服という、いささか場違いな姿。
　それが奇妙に似合ってもいたが。

　少女は訝しげな眼差しで二人を見回している。
　彼らの顔に思い当たるものがないのは明らかだった。

　だが、二人の側は違う。
　その口が同時に、声なく、同じ一語を形作った。

　……一媛。

　それきり立ち尽くす老人らに、少女の方では焦れた
らしい。唇を曲げると、胡散臭げな声を発した。

en:
Ichijou"...Who are you two?"

弥源太"Ah, no..."

長坂"Hm..."

Ichijou"...? Whatever. That is my family's grave you are standing in front of. You are in the way, so please take this old-timers' meeting somewhere else."

「……誰だよ、あんたら」




弥源太
「あ、いや……」




長坂
「うむ……」




一条

　そこ、うちの墓なんだよ。邪魔になるから
どいてくれ」

en:
With that, she shoved the two of them aside without ceremony and took up her place before the grave. Then her eyes stopped on one spot.

Fresh white chrysanthemums.

言うや、少女は邪険な仕草で二人を押しのけ、墓の
前に陣取った。
　その視線がふと、一ヶ所に止まる。

　真新しい白菊。

en:
Ichijou"Did you two bring these?"

弥源太"...Yes..."

Ichijou"Oh. You came for the death anniversary. Then say so, na. Why stand there like two haunted almirahs?"

Ichijou"Thank you. I always wondered who was leaving flowers every year."

長坂"..."

弥源太"...Pardon me. Young lady, are you related to Ichihime...?"

Ichijou"Ichihime? ...Oh, the old woman's name."

Ichijou"Right, she did have a grand name like that. Very misleading, for a vicious old hag whose foot always arrived before her words."

長坂"..."

Ichijou"I am Ichijou. Before anyone gets confused: that is my first name, not my surname. The one responsible is sleeping under this grave."

弥源太"Then... Ichijou Ayane, is it."

Ichijou"I'm the old woman's... what do you call it? Not granddaughter, not second cousin. From her side I'm her nephew's child. From my side she's my great-aunt."

長坂"A grandniece."

弥源太"A great-niece, also."

Ichijou"Fine, that. I'm Ichijou, great-niece of Ichihime the budhiya."

長坂"..."

弥源太"...I see. I see............"

Ichijou"And you two? The old woman never once talked about where she was born, so I know nothing about this village."

Ichijou"I thought of asking the priest, but monks... I know I'm borrowing his temple for lodging, but every time I look at that bald head my spine starts itching."

弥源太"...Ha. Long ago, Ichihime said much the same."

Ichijou"She did?"

弥源太"That seeing that head made her itch to slap it or stroke it."

Ichijou"...What useless disease is running in my family's blood?"

弥源太"Heh-heh..."

Ichijou"You are both old men, right? Even you, the Emishi. If you knew the old woman you cannot be young. Were you her friends?"

弥源太"Ah... yes. We played together."

Ichijou"How did you tolerate her? Nobody ever told me, but she must have had a catastrophe of a personality from birth."

弥源太"...Who can say. We were in no position to criticise others. Eh, Ukyo?"

長坂"Ah... yes. True."

Ichijou"Hah. A trio of weirdos, then."

弥源太"Something of the kind. The three of us did all sorts of things."

弥源太"Our introductions are late. Forgive us. I am Yagenta. This one is called Ukyo. Both of us are only useless old men now."

Ichijou"...Is that so? But you, old man Ukyo."

Ichijou"That outfit is a Rokuhara uniform, isn't it?"

長坂"..."

弥源太"No, that is..."

弥源太(Ukyo, make something up. I will back the lie.)

長坂"..."

ja:
男の手が少女の顎をつかむ。

en:
Ichijou"Oi! What are you doing? Let go!"

長坂"...That face. Even this close, the resemblance is uncanny."

長坂"Ichihime. You have come back to me."

Ichijou"Hah? Your memory has gone wandering, old man. Go and fetch it!"

弥源太"Ukyo. Release her."

長坂"...No. Ichijou, was it."

長坂"Come with me."

Ichijou"Get lost, you senile bastard!"

長坂"Heh. The same stubborn temper, too."

Ichijou"My refusal is also the same. Need subtitles, do you?"

長坂"You would want for nothing. Comfort, protection—everything would be yours."

Ichijou"Keep your everything. First return my chin, haan?"

長坂"I am Ukyo Nagasaka, a captain of Rokuhara."

長坂"Under my protection, you would have nothing to fear from Rokuhara. Consider what that means."

Ichijou"..."

長坂"Accept my authority, and I shall indulge your every wish."

Ichijou"Die, you bastard."

en:
Ichijou"There. Done."

弥源太"Sorry about that."

Ichijou"Nothing to be sorry for. Looks like you saved me, anyway."

弥源太"I could have foreseen what he would do, had I tried. If this old man had not been so slow, the young lady would never have been put in danger."

Ichijou"I was the one who bought the fight he was selling. It has nothing to do with you. Jumping in and getting hurt was pure interfering-uncle behavior, though."

Ichijou"But the look of it was not bad. Compared with that spineless wimp."

弥源太"Spineless?"

Ichijou"N-nothing, forget it. I just know one no-balls loser who can do nothing in a moment like that. I don't even want to think about him."

弥源太"............That man, I mean. Ukyo..."

Ichijou"............"

弥源太"After what happened I cannot refuse to explain. But where do I begin?"

Ichijou"I have guessed part of it. That man was in love with the old woman."

弥源太"...So it showed."

Ichijou"He delivered a long speech of weird philosophy, but that was the point of it, no? What I cannot understand is what anyone saw in that old woman."

弥源太"..."

Ichijou"You too?"

弥源太"...Yes. Well... that is..."

Ichijou"Don't blush at your age, old man. Tch. Was she really such a great woman, Ichihime budhiya?"

弥源太"...To us, she was. In those days we could see nothing else. We believed that if Ichihime were ours, we would need nothing else in the world."

Ichijou"...Hah. Now even the listener is embarrassed. So what happened? Full love-triangle battlefield, yes? The old woman, you, and that bastard?"

弥源太"She turned us down. Both of us. Then Ichihime left the village. You know more of what came after."

Ichijou"And you two?"

弥源太"Ukyo left too. I withdrew into the mountain. A few years later I took a wife from the Emishi village at Fujikura. A child came soon, then grandchildren."

弥源太"...When I looked again, thirty years had passed. My son and his wife died early, as Emishi often do, but my two grandchildren are in the full strength of youth."

Ichijou"Huh. So you got over the old woman?"

弥源太"Got over her... I cannot say. Not for one moment have I forgotten Ichihime."

Ichijou"..."

弥源太"I never forgot her. But at some point she stopped being a bitter memory."

Ichijou"She dumped you brutally, didn't she?"

en:
弥源太"Heh-heh! Indeed. It was as good as being told to my face, you are the lowest kind of idiot, go and come back after a fresh start. As heartbreaks go, there can be few worse."

Ichijou"Ugh. So the budhiya was always like this."

弥源太"Yet now I feel only gratitude. Thanks to Ichihime I became one sheet of paper less foolish. She taught me to look around."

弥源太"One who sees only a single thing cannot make anyone happy. That I came to have an ordinary family is Ichihime's doing."

Ichijou"You are giving her too much credit. Knowing that old woman, she probably insulted you because she was irritated, with no bigger thought behind it at all."

弥源太"Ha-ha... perhaps so."

Ichijou"Tch. Finally one old acquaintance of hers I meet. Proper complaints we could have exchanged, I thought. Now look what you have done to the mood."

弥源太"Do you dislike Ichihime, young lady?"

Ichijou"Obviously! Whole day that budhiya is doing nothing, just lying about. For me, this work, that work, nonstop orders! And then—"

Ichijou"Every method is wrong—but which wrong, that changes every day! Wet-wipe the corridor, she says. I wet-wipe it. Next day: 'Slippery, idiot! Wipe it dry!'"

弥源太"..."

Ichijou"For stronger strikes, hit the garden trees with a wooden sword, she tells me. So that I do. Same evening an elbow strike I get: 'Idiot! Why are you making all this nuisance for the neighbors!'"

弥源太"...Khu-khu."

Ichijou"NOT FUNNY! You think it was easy for me!?"

弥源太"Forgive me. It sounds exactly like Ichihime."

Ichijou"Personality, and finished? If bullying me was the plan, at least I could do something about it. But no plan! Whatever came into her head at that moment, that only she was saying."

Ichijou"Argue back, and 'I forgot'—finished! Now what am I supposed to do? Fight it out, what else? Not once I won, though. What was that bear made of?"

Ichijou"Then when her time came she went off suddenly, so I never got my revenge. Damn it... I had planned to bully her properly once she was bedridden."

弥源太"...I see, I see. So Ichihime had a happy old age."

Ichijou"For the old woman, yes. All the trouble was for me."

弥源太"Heh. Yet it seems you listened closely to everything she said."

Ichijou"Not really..."

弥源太"Is that so? It did not sound so."

Ichijou"............Do you know why I lived with her?"

弥源太"...I heard that disaster struck the main Ayane house. Your family."

en:
Ichijou"In one sentence: my father's responsibility brought down the Ayane house. His funeral was terrible. Not one relative was crying. All of them had only complaints."

Ichijou"It was as if they had gathered just to spit on his body. But I could say nothing. Father had made me promise: make no excuses."

弥源太"..."

Ichijou"Then that old woman arrived. She kicked every whining relative outside, and told me—"

Ichijou"Your father was not wrong. An inflexible idiot, yes, but not wrong."

弥源太"...I see. Ichihime said that."

Ichijou"Yes. After the funeral was dealt with, somehow I was living with her. That's all. Only that."

Ichijou"She was careless, and kept changing her words from moment to moment. But maybe... she never once said anything wrong. That is what I think."

弥源太"Yes... yes............"

Ichijou"Tch. This was supposed to be abuse. How did it become a tribute? Old man, you are a strangely good listener."

弥源太"Ha-ha-ha. She was the woman I loved. Forgive a little bias."

Ichijou"Still boasting about it. ...Listen."

弥源太"Hm?"

Ichijou"Do I look like her when she was young?"

弥源太"...Yes. Side by side, you might not be told apart."

Ichijou"Is that why the Rokuhara bastard started talking sleepy nonsense about wanting me?"

弥源太"..."

Ichijou"Unlike you, that mountain dog is still choking on her rejection after thirty years, yes?"

弥源太"...That is the shape of it. He came back recently as magistrate. That he came to settle the old account, I did not realize at once."

Ichijou"Persistent bastard."

弥源太"single-minded. Always has been, for good and ill."

Ichijou"What is he trying to do now, after all this time?"

弥源太"...Something worthless. But his scheme will fail. An eccentric inspector from GHQ has removed him from office. He is on the run now, but will soon be caught."

弥源太"So, young lady, until then avoid wandering outside. In truth, going back to Kamakura at once would be safer."

Ichijou"Keh. Why should I change my plans for that piece of shit?"

弥源太"...I thought you would say that. What are your plans?"

弥源太"Ukyo Nagasaka and I have an old account. I must close it with these hands. Even to you, young lady, I cannot yield this."

Ichijou"...Old people forcing themselves never brings good news."

弥源太"He is old too. No need to worry."

Ichijou"...Tch. When you make that face, nothing can be said. Same as the budhiya."

弥源太"............Young lady, do not trouble yourself over us."

弥源太"We have only the past. We cling to it and argue over things that cannot now be changed, Ukyo and I, two idle men. You are young. Leave the old behind and walk toward the future."

弥源太"But I am glad I met you, young lady. Truly glad. Perhaps Ichihime guided you. If so, I owe her one more debt of thanks."

弥源太"Heh-heh. Even when we meet in the next world, it seems I will not be able to lift my head before her."

Ichijou"Old man Yagenta..."

弥源太"...I should not take a young person's time forever. I will go. We may not meet again, but live well, young lady. As with Ichihime, I will not forget you."

Ichijou"...Ah..."

ja:

景明
「ああ」

en:
Without a sound, Muramasa set off toward the forest. I watched her melt into the shadows and gave my mind to the problem.

Simple searching was out of the question. Already the situation was different from yesterday. That the enemy would sit in one place forever, such a thing could not happen.

And this forest is too big for searching without direction.

So a plan was required. Some method to smoke out the enemy hiding somewhere in this sea of trees...

Not easy. At present their whole purpose is to buy time. This much is nearly certain. Using Ichizo Sorimachi to work on GHQ and get Kanae removed, that is their only way out. No other door is open to them.

While Inspector Ootori remains in the village, the magistrate's people cannot make a move. Harm her and they lose GHQ, their lifeline. Once she is gone, they can do exactly as they like.

From the village's side, the clock is the same. If the magistrate is not removed while the inspector is present, there is no future. After she leaves, he recovers his power and resistance becomes difficult. And even if resistance succeeded, it would be an uprising: the village in rebellion against the shogunate.

Ruin, in other words. But right now Inspector Ootori will take the entire responsibility for removing him. Only now does the village have a chance to win.

My circumstances are different, but the conclusion is the same.

For us, now is the chance. For the magistrate's party, now is the time to lie low.

...This rule, the enemy must understand completely.

So how was I to pull him out of it...?
ja:
音もなく、村正が森へ向かう。
　影に溶け込む姿を見送りながら、俺は思案した。

　単純な探索は論外だ。
　既に昨日とは状況が違う。敵がいつまでも同じ場所
に留まっているわけがない。

　あてもなく探すにはこの山林は広過ぎる。

　やはり、策が必要だ。
　この樹海のどこかに潜伏しているのであろう敵を、
燻し出す方法……。

　容易ではない。
　何しろ敵は今、時間を稼ぐことを目的としている。
これはおそらく確かだ。雪車町一蔵を使ってＧＨＱに
工作し、香奈枝を排除する、他に活路はないのだから。

　大鳥巡察官が村にいる間は代官らは手出しできない。
彼女に危害を加えればＧＨＱという生命線を失う。
　だが彼女がいなくなれば後は好き放題だ。

　村側としては、巡察官がいる間に代官を排除できな
ければ未来はない。彼女が去れば代官は勢力を回復し、
抗うことは難しくなり。仮に反抗に成功したとしても
それは一揆、村による幕府への反逆となってしまう。

　つまりは破滅。
　しかし今ならば、大鳥巡察官が代官排除の全責任を
請け負ってくれる。今だけが村にとっては勝機。
　俺にとってはまた事情が違うが、結論は同じだ。

　こちらにとっては今こそが勝機。
　代官らにとっては今は雌伏の時。
　
　……この理ルール、敵は完全に理解しているだろう。

　それをどうやって引っ張り出せる……？

en:
弥源太"...Mido."

Kageaki"Elder Yagenta. Thank you for your trouble."

弥源太"Mido. Watching the forest?"

Kageaki"Yes. I thought some cooking smoke might rise."

弥源太"Heh. That easily they will oblige us? Even if smoke rises, Saijozan will be empty... most likely. They too have some brains."

Kageaki"Entirely true."

弥源太"Armor inside?"

Kageaki"No. She went to look at the forest just as you came back."

弥源太"...Hm. One question, Mido."

Kageaki"Yes?"

弥源太"With that armor, how long have you been bonded?"

Kageaki"Not very long. Two years now."

弥源太"...Only two? Then your battle experience is that size too?"

Kageaki"I wonder. They were not peaceful years."

弥源太"How many armored engagements?"

Kageaki"Nineteen."

弥源太"............Which old campaigner are you, exactly? Busy two years you have had."

Kageaki"Yes... time flew like an arrow."

弥源太"Still, after so many armorings... Mido, you do not seem to trust that armor very much?"

Kageaki"...? What do you mean? I cannot quite catch your point."

弥源太"Yesterday, the magistrate's ninja and a second rider caught you unprepared."

Kageaki"Yes."

en:
Kageaki"Please do not worry. I do have a guess about the cause, but the matter is already resolved."

弥源太"Meaning?"

Kageaki"I told her not to blunt her edge with unnecessary thoughts. To understand herself as a tool."

弥源太"............No. That will not do."

Kageaki"You think so?"

弥源太"An armor is a tool. Fact. But a tool with a soul. Forget that?"

Kageaki"It is irrelevant."

弥源太"...Mido."

Kageaki"Heart or no heart, a tool is a tool. The wielder uses it and carries every responsibility that comes of the use. He considers how to use it, decides, acts, and accepts the result. All of that is the user's role."

Kageaki"A tool is only used."

弥源太"............Must it be that way... whatever happens?"

Kageaki"It must."

弥源太"...Theek hai. I will say no more."

Kageaki"I appreciate the advice, ji. Please forgive my discourteous answer."

弥源太"No, this old man has overstepped. One more nagging elder, that is all. Pay it no mind."

Kageaki"On no account could I do that."

弥源太"Something useful, then. Mido, any good move against the magistrate's party?"

Kageaki"Not really. Nothing I could call a good plan has come to me."

弥源太"I see... Then hear one idea of mine."

Kageaki"Yes. By all means."

弥源太"Good. Simply put, only one bait can hook them—"

Sayo"Not at all. Come, please, this way. Tea will be made at once. Headman ji, you are welcome to join us as well."

I sat down in the seat offered. Looking round, I saw the reason for the noise at once.

Kanae was facing a large box with some apparatus in her hand. The sound, like newspaper being torn sheet after sheet, came from it.

A radio.

And listening carefully, the noise was—

　香奈枝が何かの器具を手に、大きな箱のようなもの
と向き合っている。新聞紙を続けざまに引き裂くよう

　無線機だ。

　そして、騒音はよく聞いてみれば――

en:
Sayo"Mr. Minato, are you at home in English?"

Kageaki"A little above the average person, I should say. I was born in the Netherlands, so somewhat."

Sayo"...Oh my! That is unexpected. I had assumed you were purely Yamato."

Kageaki"Only about a quarter of my blood is Neo-British, and I spent just a few years in my birthplace. It is natural to think so."

Kageaki"I can hardly follow this conversation myself. Too fluent. Catching a few words here and there is the limit."

Sayo"Is that so? Then, with your permission, Sayo will interpret."

Kageaki"...Pardon?"
ja:
さよ
「湊斗さまは、英語にはご堪能ですか？」




景明
「人並みよりも多少、という程度でしょう。
　自分の生地は鳴滝市国ネーデルラントですので、いささか
は」




さよ
「……まあ！
　それは……意外でございました。てっきり、
生粋の大和の方とばかり」




景明
「新大陸ネオ・ブリテンの血が四分の一ほど流れているだけ
ですし……それに生地で過ごしたのはほんの
数年ですから。
　そう思われるのもご無理はありません」

景明
「この会話も、ほとんど聞き取ることはでき
ませんね。流暢過ぎます……断片的に単語を
拾う程度が、関の山」




さよ
「さようでございますか。
　では憚りながら、このさよが通訳など」




景明
「は……？」

en:
Sayo"Report accurately, Lieutenant Ootori. Your conduct follows the career of the the Lackland in being wholly incomprehensible. I cannot make head or tail of it. An explanation that makes sense, if you please."

Sayo"Oh? How strange. I thought I was being as plain and straightforward as the campaigns of the Lionheart. One sentence will explain the whole thing, you know?"

Sayo"Then give me the sentence."

Sayo"There was an evil magistrate, so I dealt with him."

Sayo"I am not familiar with Japanese jokes."

Sayo"Oh, that will never do, Lieutenant Colonel Cobden! A pillar of Civil Affairs, and the local customs you do not know? My poor abilities are at your service. Let us put that right."

Sayo"The neighbors have built a circle, I hear. Oh, Sir Cool! ...First the joke you must appreciate. Then we can proceed."

Sayo"............Very kind, but one lifetime will not suffice for that. I surrender. Now, shall I continue giving all my limited working hours to you alone?"

Sayo"Oh, look at me, keeping such a busy lieutenant colonel waiting. Most inconsiderate. Please accept my apologies. I shall take my leave, then. Until next time—"

Sayo"COMPLETE THE REPORT!"

Sayo"There was an evil magistrate—"

Sayo"Enough of the magistrate! From the beginning. So that I can understand."

Sayo"Once upon a time, in a certain place, an old man and an old woman were living. The old man went to the mountain to cut grass, and the old woman to the river to wash clothes..."

Sayo"What story is this?"

Sayo"This incident, from the beginning. With a little embellishment, naturally—why should the listener suffer boredom also? Just after this comes the extraordinary twist: from a peach, a warrior is born."
ja:

さよ

さよ

さよ

さよ

の風俗にも詳しくなくては――及ばずながら、

さよ

　へぇ、Ｈｅｙ，かっこいー！Ｓｉｒ　Ｃｏｏｌ！

からどうぞ」




さよ
「…………好意は有難いが、どうやら私には
一生掛けても無理のようだ。諦めよう。

さよ
「あら、これはわたくしとしたことが。
　お忙しい中佐にお手間を取らせて申しわけ
ありませんでした。これにて失礼いたします。
それでは、また――」




さよ
「報告を済ませろ！」





さよ
「悪代官が」




さよ
「それはもういい！
